method: Source/issue reconciliation and retained-evidence extraction only; no new full audit or benchmarks. Issue states unchanged.

windows_regression.scope: Existing native Windows CI log; no rerun. Interactive Ctrl+C not newly validated.

records.title: Windows watch children after force-kill
records.assessment: Windows watch launches now use a native helper instead of the MSYS2 setsid branch. The helper owns a kill-on-close Windows Job Object, launches the server suspended, assigns it before resuming, and waits for the exact parent process. Both app and build-error servers use this path.
records.proposal: Propose closing #275 for the reported force-kill orphan/port leak: both native watch-child modes have a passing Windows lifetime regression on the released tree. Keep interactive console Ctrl+C behavior and broader Windows production supervision with the Windows owner; this proposal does not certify those separate contracts.
records.limit: Windows preview run 40601183776 logs this named regression, followed by all four runtime-parity tests passing. Its synthetic merge 700e27861cd9328f3fa1fdd0be669e53badd8818 has the same tree as main. No Windows fixture/design changes or new native tests were made here.

records.title: File-backed queue duplication, lost updates and shared default path
records.assessment: ALNFileJobAdapter takes an exclusive sibling .lock around reload/mutate/persist operations, including initialization and leases. The queue-jobs generator uses `<app-root>/var/jobs/state.plist` instead of a shared temporary directory and fails registration if initialization fails. Generated timers can still run in multiple HTTP workers because queue claims now coordinate.
records.proposal: Propose closing #282 for concurrent file-queue duplicate leasing/lost enqueues and the cross-app default-path collision. The retained regressions cover independent producers/consumers and interleaved transactions. Use PostgreSQL/dedicated jobs workers when crashed-lease recovery is required.
records.limit: The file adapter still has no crashed-worker lease recovery or exactly-once side-effect guarantee. Moving every generated timer to a dedicated worker is an architectural option, not a prerequisite for the specific locking fix. Existing generated apps must regenerate or adopt the new template.

records.title: Shared module state and doctor warning
records.assessment: The reported notification preference/inbox lost updates are addressed by authoritative shared state and SQLite catalog transactions. Jobs operator state, search module state and ops history use cross-process reload/mutate/commit paths. Both doctor entrypoints now require state.durable=YES or one worker; a database URL alone no longer silences the warning. The default pending-job adapter remains ALNInMemoryJobAdapter, so pending jobs are still process-local until an application selects a shared adapter.
records.proposal: Keep #251 open for the remaining default-adapter/deployment contract, or close only after moving that residual into an explicitly reviewed follow-up. Record the notification, jobs-operator, search, ops lost-update fixes and database-URL warning fix as completed sub-items; do not describe default in-memory pending jobs as shared.
records.limit: state.durable is an operator declaration, not automatic per-module backend verification. Use one scheduler; enqueue and scheduler bookkeeping are separate. External search engine publication still needs one writer per resource or backend fencing. docs/PROPANE.md still says an existing database contract can satisfy the first warning version: that sentence is historical wording that disagrees with current doctor code/tests and merits a focused docs follow-up. No owner source was changed.

records.title: Bounded default in-memory cache and mail retention
records.assessment: The default cache now keeps at most 1,024 entries, updates LRU order on hits/writes, and sweeps expired entries when writing a non-null value. The mail adapter retains only the latest 100 deliveries. These are the two unbounded collection growth paths in the report.
records.proposal: Propose closing #283 for unbounded entry retention: the cache is capped at 1,024 LRU entries and sweeps expired entries on writes; the mail adapter retains the latest 100 deliveries. Both named regressions passed in the retained release suite.
records.limit: These are entry-count bounds, not byte caps. Up to 100 messages can retain message content, and expired cache entries can remain until another read/write. Optional startup warnings and alternative production adapters are separate improvements; do not claim that the bounded defaults are a production mail delivery service.

records.title: Prevent multiplied built-in rate budgets under propane
records.assessment: Startup now rejects enabled built-in rate limiting with more than one configured worker, including exported ARLEN_PROPANE_WORKERS/legacy overrides. Propane also refuses before launching workers. The request limiter itself remains process-local; configuration and deployment docs direct multi-worker deployments to an ingress limiter.
records.proposal: Propose closing #252 for silently multiplying a configured request budget by the propane worker count. The unsafe configuration now fails before serving or launching workers. Run one worker for the built-in limiter, or disable it and enforce the shared budget at ingress.
records.limit: This is a fail-closed configuration fix, not a shared-store limiter. Independent app instances/hosts still require an external deployment-wide quota. Authentication account limits are a separate mechanism.

records.title: Header serialization and construction cost
records.assessment: The serializer now writes NSData bytes; constant security headers are prepared once per middleware/application instance; validation uses cached character sets, and ordered insertion avoids the redundant linear containsObject scan. The later 3fa59adf construction follow-up resolves some residuals listed in the older handoff. Public setters still validate dynamic inputs. The shared serialization fast path remains restricted to its standard small header layout.
records.proposal: Keep #245 open as a performance residual, or split it before closing the completed byte-serialization and constant-header construction work. Exact wire bytes/ordering/overrides are covered. Do not present this as elimination of the original 35–40% end-to-end request CPU share.
records.limit: Release notes retain historical 1.6–2x serializer evidence; PERFORMANCE_PROFILES records Windows construction trials (32.1% middleware, 7.2% dynamic32). They are distinct historical microbenchmarks, not new measurements on e26a755e. The standard-header cache is not broadened to the full default 19-header layout. No benchmark campaign was run.

records.title: JSON logger encoding cost
records.assessment: JSON log output now passes serializer UTF-8 data to emitLogData:, appends one newline, and writes the bytes. The NSData-to-NSString-to-NSData round-trip is gone. JSON serialization and a synchronous per-logger sink lock remain, and production access logging is still enabled at the configured INFO threshold.
records.proposal: Keep #248 open for the remaining logging-cost question, or split before closing the redundant UTF-8 conversion sub-item. The targeted byte path is shipped; the retained 10–15% access-log-line improvement is not a claim that the original 25–33% request CPU overhead has disappeared.
records.limit: The original fix commit 328ce73c explicitly says partial. Existing logger regressions cover levels, bounded POSIX backpressure and text escaping; they are not a dedicated JSON byte-equivalence benchmark. Windows sink behavior remains synchronous. No asynchronous sink, lock-free queue or new performance result is claimed.

records.title: Concurrent upload 500s caused by runner temporary space exhaustion
records.assessment: The issue owner confirmed ENOSPC and explicitly made closure conditional on #203. Current Linux workflows set TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP to a private per-job on-disk runner directory; setting all three matters because GNUstep uses TEMP/TMP. The retained complete native ARM integration report executes the unchanged concurrent 20 MiB multipart/body-limit case successfully.
records.proposal: Propose closing #196: the confirmed runner ENOSPC cause is isolated by the merged per-job TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP setup, and the original both-backends concurrent upload regression passes in retained release evidence. Keep developer-machine fixture leaks tracked separately in #210.
records.limit: This does not claim all test temp leaks are fixed or that arbitrary disk-full multipart failures now return 503. The single issue comment identifies per-job temp isolation as the lasting fix; storage-pressure response policy is separate.

records.title: Clean-checkout deploy-smoke packaging
records.assessment: build_release.sh now packages tools/platform.sh and detects app_lite.m or any src/**/*.m, matching propane. Release certification runs smoke_release.sh against examples/tech_demo, and the retained full integration suite passes the release smoke/runbook regression. However, a missing compiled app still falls through to a manifest path: the promised app_binary_missing guard and specifically named non-main-source regression are absent.
records.proposal: Keep #169 open only for the missing fail-fast app_binary_missing diagnostic and explicit non-main-entry-point regression, or move those to a reviewed follow-up before closing the original packaging failures. The platform helper and broad source detection fixes are shipped, and certification now exercises the real tech_demo release smoke.
records.limit: The two existing tests do not specifically instantiate the promised no-main.m fixture; inventory/source searches find no testReleasePackagesBinaryForAppWithoutMainSource. The tagged certification is retained evidence, not a new clean-checkout deploy-smoke run in this reconciliation.

records.title: Expectation-based test waits
records.assessment: Shared ALNTestWaitUntil, ALNTestWaitForTaskExit and ALNTestWaitForTCPPort helpers exist and use XCTWaiter when available. The docs gate runs a non-increasing sleep baseline lint. The current baseline still permits eight unannotated waits in Phase24WindowsRuntimeParityTests.m; the original comment counted nine before later edits.
records.proposal: Keep #114 open for the remaining eight Windows runtime-parity waits. Shared waiter helpers, the initial conversions and the monotonic lint are complete. Ask the Windows fixture owner to convert or justify the remaining calls individually; no broad lifecycle rewrite is proposed.
records.limit: The current lint passes with eight baseline entries; that is not proof of zero sleeps. Annotated intentional delays and the toolchain fallback remain legitimate. Windows source/fixtures were read only here.

records.title: Production observability and route-catalog exposure
records.assessment: In environment=production, /metrics and /clusterz return 404 unless a token, loopback-only restriction or explicit operabilityAnonymous opt-in is configured. Token comparison is constant-time, and loopback access rejects forwarded-header proxy traffic. OpenAPI routes are unavailable outside development/test until publicInProduction is enabled.
records.proposal: Propose marking H-1 complete for production defaults and explicit access controls. Preserve the documented development/non-production behavior and operator opt-ins; do not claim every custom environment name automatically makes /metrics private.
records.limit: The old 0.3.0 release note says anonymous by default. Current source and 0.3.1 tests supersede that historical statement for environment=production. A custom environment other than production must set its observability controls explicitly.

records.title: MCP catalog authorization
records.assessment: tools/list filters required roles/scopes, assurance age and route-policy visibility without executing handlers. tools/call retains full enforcement. A deliberately roleless/scopeless tool can still be listed/called by an authenticated subject, as its declared policy allows.
records.proposal: Propose marking H-2 complete for unauthorized catalog disclosure. Tool authors must still declare requiredRoles/scopes for sensitive custom tools; a tool with no requirements is intentionally available within its enclosing authentication contract.
records.limit: Catalog filtering is not execution of arbitrary application guards or tool handlers. The regression explicitly retains public.ping for an authenticated visitor, while hidden admin/scoped calls remain denied.

records.title: Reset and verification token storage
records.assessment: New random reset/verification bearer tokens are transformed by AMStoredBearerToken before insertion; consumption looks up the digest, not the presented plaintext. Existing plaintext links are invalidated by the lookup contract and must be reissued. Single-use consumption and reset invalidation of older tokens are also covered.
records.proposal: Propose marking H-3 complete for usable plaintext bearer tokens in auth token tables. New rows contain SHA-256 digests and old plaintext links no longer redeem. Request replacement links after upgrading.
records.limit: This does not claim that mailboxes, provider delivery records, old backups or historical rows contain no plaintext. A user-facing bearer link necessarily reaches its intended recipient; this issue is the token-table account-takeover path.

records.title: Built-in auth enumeration and forgot-password mail timing
records.assessment: Unknown-email login spends an Argon2id verification; registration gives generic responses for existing and new addresses without automatic sign-in. Durable registration/forgot-password paths queue work for both address cases, with token creation and mail outside the HTTP request. Production-like local-password/mail setups reject synchronous mail and registration auto-login. Queue failure returns a generic 503; new-account creation and mail enqueue are atomic.
records.proposal: Propose marking H-4 complete for built-in production-like registration/login/forgot-password behavior, including Dan’s forgot-password timing follow-up. Apply the auth/jobs migrations, configure durable jobs/publicBaseURL and run its worker. Preserve separate review of app-owned registration hooks and explicitly enabled development compatibility modes.
records.limit: The request still performs a durable enqueue and registration database work; this is not a zero-latency or mathematically constant-time claim. Custom hooks may reveal timing. Historical 0.3.0 synchronous-mode wording was superseded by the 0.3.1 startup rejection.

records.title: Replayed SMS cookie attempt counters
records.assessment: The cookie still carries UI/session counters, but both SMS send and verification reserve an account-scoped attempt in the database before invoking the provider. They fail closed if the attempt-limit schema is unavailable. This addresses the identified trust boundary in source. No dedicated regression that replays a stale SMS cookie through those two flows was found in the pinned test inventory/source or selected retained release evidence.
records.proposal: Keep H-5 open as a narrow verification follow-up: retain the implemented server-side SMS attempt reservations, then add a stale-cookie replay regression for sends and failed verifies proving provider calls remain bounded across sessions/workers and missing-schema handling fails closed. This reconciliation does not assert the old bypass still reproduces.
records.limit: Generic TOTP/account-limit and SMS management tests are related coverage, not direct proof of stale SMS-cookie resistance. No external SMS calls, new fixtures or full audit were run; source review alone is not labeled end-to-end replay validation.

records.title: Notification inbox link schemes
records.assessment: NMSafeInboxHref accepts http/https URLs with a host or relative paths, rejecting controls, backslashes, protocol-relative links and other schemes. The controller places only the sanitized linkHref into display entries; the HTML template emits a link only when that field is nonempty.
records.proposal: Propose marking H-6 complete for unsafe link schemes in the HTML inbox. Non-http(s) schemes render without a link; the integration regression exercises safe and unsafe destinations.
records.limit: External http/https links remain allowed by design. This is a scheme-safety rule, not a same-origin-only destination allowlist.

records.title: PostgreSQL autocomplete LIKE wildcards
records.assessment: STEscapedLikePattern escapes backslash, percent and underscore before appending the intended prefix wildcard. Both LIKE clauses declare the escape character and continue to use bound parameters/resource scope.
records.proposal: Propose marking H-7 complete: user-supplied percent/underscore/backslash are literal in the PostgreSQL prefix LIKE pattern. The retained native normal suite executes the PostgreSQL wildcard regression without skipping it.
records.limit: Fuzzy/trigram matching remains intentional in the alternative branch; the fix is not removal of every broad search behavior. ALNSearchModule was read only, and no search benchmarking or owner changes were made.
